sections.content: How many people are "pharmacy and optical dispensing assistants"?

75,980 people

were counted on the census as "pharmacy and optical dispensing assistants" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Pharmacy and optical dispensing assistants work under the supervision of pharmacists and opticians or optometrists to dispense drugs and medicines, issue pre-packaged prescriptions, sell over-the-counter medication, dispense spectacles and contact lenses and other related products.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "pharmacy and optical dispensing assistants" there were more women than men (86.9% compared with 13.1%).

This means "pharmacy and optical dispensing assistants" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "sales occupations".

Men made up 13.1% and women made up 86.9% of "pharmacy and optical dispensing assistants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "pharmacy and optical dispensing assistants" included:

  • other registered nursing professionals
  • health care practice managers
  • special and additional needs education teaching professionals

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "pharmacy and optical dispensing assistants", 14.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "pharmacy and optical dispensing assistants" was 65 years or older.

We can look at who worked as "pharmacy and optical dispensing assistants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "pharmacy and optical dispensing assistants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "pharmacy and optical dispensing assistants", 11.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (54.5% compared with 45.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98.5%) than self-employed (1.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
